notes: The ground of the Reach changes as you cross it — pale scoured stone in one stretch, dark burnt crust in another. The great rock the starting cave is cut into never got the message. It wore the same warm brown everywhere, so walking out of the cave mouth onto pale ground left a rock face standing over you that belonged somewhere else entirely.
That rock now takes its colouring from the ground it actually stands on. Where the mouth opens onto the pale scoured flats, the face above it is pale too.

It is not one flat repaint. The rock is broad enough to stand in two kinds of ground at once, so it shades between them across its face the same way the ground does underfoot. The leaning slabs framing the cave mouth follow the same ground, so the doorway does not stay warm against a rock face that has gone pale.
Inside the cave nothing has changed. Those walls are lit by torchlight rather than by the sky, and the weather still stops at the mouth.

This is a step and not the finished thing. The haze and low sun of the Reach swallow most of any difference in colour before it reaches your eye, and the rock is usually seen from far off, so the change is real but quiet — clearest standing near it, faint on the skyline. The rock also follows the ground's brightness more than its exact colour, and it is still one smooth stone surface: no thickness, rubble or broken faces yet.
title: The starting rock belongs to the ground it stands on
